title: Good circuit decisions exclude bad specifications
statement:
Let $C,c	ext{ in } acks lash	extbackslash N$, let $V$ be a language of bit strings, and let $F$ be a family of acyclic Boolean circuits with at most two inputs per gate, with well-formed gates, one circuit for each input length. Suppose the language accepted by $F$ is the language of strings $q$ for which, writing $(x,y)$ for the decoded pair components of $q$, there is a suffix $s$ such that $|y' s|=C(|x|+1)^c$ and $ g x,y's g	ext{ belongs to }V$, where $y'$ is obtained by deleting the marker from $y$. For bit strings $x,U$, suppose deleting the marker from $U$ gives the encoding of the circuit in $F$ on input length $2(2|x|+2+C(|x|+1)^c)+2+(C(|x|+1)^c+1)$. Suppose also that for every $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^c$ there is a $v$ of that same length with $ g g x,u g,v g	ext{ belongs to }V$. Then for every bit strings $u,j,p$ it is not the case that all three length bounds $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$, $|j|\le C(|x|+1)^c$, $|p|\le C(|x|+1)^c$ hold together with at least one of these: the corresponding circuit query on $ g x,u g$ rejects the all-ones marker; $|p|=C(|x|+1)^c$ and the query on $0p$ accepts while $ g g x,p g
otin V$; or $|j|+|p|+1=C(|x|+1)^c$, the query on $1 0 p$ preceded by $|j|$ ones accepts, and both queries formed by preceding $0(p0)$ and $0(p1)$ by $|j|$ ones reject. Here $ g a,b g$ denotes the encoding of a pair, and each query uses the circuit code obtained by deleting the marker from $U$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a family whose circuits have well-formed gates and fan-in at most two
The accepted language of $F$ equals the specified prefix language
The marker-deleted $U$ is the encoded circuit for the specified input length
For every length-$C(|x|+1)^c$ string $u$, a same-length witness $v$ makes the paired string belong to $V$
caveat: The statement expands several nested encodings and predicates; the exact decoding and marker conventions are compressed into the prose.
